explanation: The calendar counts from AD 622, when Muhammad and his followers migrated to Medina, an event called the Hijra. Its months follow the Moon, so its years run about 11 days shorter than solar ones.

claims.text: Year 1 of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar is the year of the Hijra, Muhammad's migration to Medina.
The Islamic calendar does not count its years from Muhammad's birth, the first revelation or the Battle of Badr.
The Hijra took place in AD 622.
The months of the Islamic calendar are lunar.
An Islamic calendar year is about 11 days shorter than a solar year.
